subject: Re: MRDS - using fitted detection function from previous analysis

messages.author: 12f269733c6eb9a2
messages.subject: Re: MRDS - using fitted detection function from previous analysis
parts:
Alistair:

I'm poking about in the bowls of the Distance code looking for the spot
where the error message you describe is generated. Unfortunately, I'm
not finding exactly the message you describe, but I have found some
things that are close approximations.

Is the error message

"Could not find 'Detection' command in Model definition"

Might you be able to send along the script that you captured when in
debug mode; that may help in ferreting out the difficulty you are having.

Alistair Stewart wrote:
> > Hi all,
> >
> > I am having difficulty using MRDS to estimate density / abundance from
> > a fitted detection function of a previous MRDS analysis using Distance
> > 5 release 2.
> >
> > I am using MRDS to fit a detection function to a larger dataset to
> > predict detection probabilities in a smaller dataset to estimate the
> > densitiy and abundance. This is covered in the Distance 5.0 release 2
> > user's guide in chapter 10, p137. So far I have been able to run the
> > initial MRDS model and retain the R data file for the following
> > analysis that uses the R output for the model definition.
> >
> > I am receiving the following error in the log when I attempt to run
> > the second estimate density / abundance from a fitted detection
> > function of a previous MRDS analysis:
> > ** Error: Could not find the Method command in the model definition. **
> >
> > I have checked and reinstalled the R package 2.4.1 that is currently
> > supported for use with the MRDS library. I have reinstalled Distance
> > 5.0 release 2 and checked the settings for use with R according to the
> > user's guide. I have checked the .RData workspace to make sure the
> > data is there for further analyses and it appears to be there. I have
> > run the MRDS using the debug mode for script logging and it works for
> > the initial MRDS analysis but halts on the second 'estimate density /
> > abundance from a fitted detection function of a previous MRDS' analysis.
> >
> > Has anyone got any ideas why it is not working for me? Or
> > alternatively, is there a script that I could follow or adapt to use
> > in R for MRDS using a previously fitted detection function? I have
> > little experience in scripting for R but am willing to pull it all
> > apart and start learning for this one.
> >
> > I have had a search in the archives and haven't found anyhting yet,
> > but apologies if it has already been covered.
> >
> > Cheers,
> >
> > Alistair
> >

messages.author: 5900eadecec2d82d
messages.subject: Re: MRDS - using fitted detection function from previous analysis
parts:
Hi All,

I have found and fixed the bug that Alistair and others noted, together=20
with another related bug in the MRDS interface code. I have uploaded a=20
patch to Distance 5.0 Release 2 that implements the fix. You can=20
download it from
http://www.ruwpa.st-and.ac.uk/distance/downloads/d5r2patch.zip

Unzip the file, and follow the instructions in ReadMe.txt.

I have also patched the Distance 5.0 Release 2 setup file, so that=20
anyone downloading Distance 5.0 after today will get the patched version.

Thanks again for pointing out the bug.

- Len Thomas

The fixed bugs are:
=B7 {355} Cannot deal with missing distances in interval data. Error is=20
in create.interval.data function. [Fixed LJT 9 Jan 2008]
=B7 {356} When running analyses using previous detection functions, get=20
error =93Could not find the method command in model definition=94. [Fixe=
d=20
LJT 9 Jan 2008]

--=20

The Observatory, University of St Andrews, Scotland KY16 9LZ
